text:
jen-encops: FYI found a set of nightly DB backups in aws://redwood-archive/old-backups/ that appear to be stored without CMEK (SSE-S3 only). file list shows ~2021-2022 snapshots.

sam-sre: whoa, how did those get there? we thought backup-agent always used customer CMKs.

jen-encops: looks like the old backup uploader service (svc-backup-v1) was using SSE-S3 before we rolled out CMEK enforcement in 2023. CloudTrail shows PutObject events from that principal.

raj-sec: any restore attempts failing? could be related to the CMK rotation we did last week if they were CMEK, but you said SSE-S3 so keys wouldn't be involved. need to confirm encryption mode per object headers (x-amz-server-side-encryption).

mike-db: I'll run a quick head-object on a few. cmd: `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-archive --key old-backups/db-2021-07-01.dump` and check `ServerSideEncryption` and `SSEKMSKeyId`.

backup-bot: Alert: bucket redwood-archive had 3 PutObject events from svc-backup-v1 on 2021-07-01. No PutBucketEncryption API calls found for that period. :information_source:

sam-sre: If objects are SSE-S3 (no KMS key) then they're encrypted by AWS-managed S3 key. that's still "encrypted at rest" but not customer-managed CMK for recovery/audit. we need to treat this as policy drift and potential compliance gap.

jen-encops: Confirmed — head-object returns `ServerSideEncryption: AES256` and no `SSEKMSKeyId`.

raj-sec: Ok — compliance impact: these backups are not under customer CMK/escrow; may not meet some regs. Action plan: (1) inventory all objects in that prefix older than 2023, (2) snapshot access audit (who downloaded), (3) decide to re-encrypt or delete/retain, (4) update RBAC and automation to prevent recurrence.

sam-sre: For inventory: run `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-archive --prefix old-backups/ --query 'Contents[?LastModified<`2023-01-01`].[Key,LastModified]'` and save to SSM parameter store or secure bucket.

mike-db: For re-encryption: can't change SSE-S3 objects to SSE-KMS in-place. options: copy object to same key with `--sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <cmk>` (recommended) or export, encrypt locally, re-upload. copying will create new PutObject; need to ensure IAM principal performing copy has kms:Encrypt on target CMK.

raj-sec: Important RBAC note: backup-agent service account no longer exists for v1. if we create a one-off migration job, grant temporary permissions via ephemeral role (sts:AssumeRole) and record CloudTrail grant events. No permanent IAM change without approvals.

jen-encops: Also saw some restores in 2022 by user `ops_jenny` — we should check whether those downloads included sensitive tenants. will pull object-level access logs and S3 access logs.

sam-sre: Last week CMK rotation caused one restore to fail for a test tenant because a grant expired on an ephemeral decrypt grant. different issue but related: make sure any re-encryption job creates new CMK grants and sets proper grant tokens if needed.

raj-sec: Audit logging: enable S3 data events in CloudTrail for that bucket (if not already) and add Athena query to list GetObject events filtered by `old-backups/`. retention: move logs to secured audit bucket.

mike-db: I can run a small POC: copy one object to `old-backups-reencrypted/2021-07-01.dump` with `--copy-source` and `--sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/...`. will validate a restore from that copy.

jen-encops: Please also add a tag on re-encrypted objects `re-encrypted-by=encops` and add a manifest file with original etag + sha256 so we can prove fidelity.

sam-sre: For compliance decision, security should recommend either (A) re-encrypt all pre-2023 objects with our CMK and keep, or (B) if retention policy allows, delete older ones and document rationale. lean towards re-encrypt until legal signs off.

raj-sec: I'll draft a short incident advisory: describe scope (count of objects, timeframe), risk (not under CMEK), actions taken (inventory, re-encryption POC, RBAC lock-down), and next steps (policy enforcement and audit enablement). need approval from legal & compliance.

backup-bot: Note: creating copy with KMS will generate KMS GenerateDataKey and Encrypt API calls — will show up in KMS audit logs. ensure that KMS key policy allows the ephemeral migration role and logs are forwarded to Splunk.

mike-db: POC done — copy succeeded, restore verified against checksum. no decrypt errors. I used ephemeral migration role with kms:Encrypt and s3:PutObject.

jen-encops: Great. Next: (1) run inventory scan and attach manifest to ticket, (2) schedule bulk re-encrypt during low-traffic window with rate limits to avoid KMS throttle, (3) lock svc-backup-v1 principal fully and add explicit deny for PutObject until codepath removed, (4) add bucket policy to require SSE-KMS with our CMK for that prefix.

sam-sre: KMS throttling note: for large bulk ops, use multiple keys or batch with exponential backoff. document expected KMS request rate and open a support case if we need increased quotas.

raj-sec: I'll prepare the advisory and request legal/compliance review. please attach CloudTrail evidence and the manifest when ready. keep me CC'd.

jen-encops: tagging @raj-sec in the ticket. thanks everyone. closing thread once advisory posted and inventory file uploaded. :white_check_mark:
